reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Regulating big tech oligarchs
themes.definition: Critique of a handful of tech oligarchs and big techs pursuing unregulated digital ultra-liberalism, bypassing the UN, and pressure from multinationals on national sovereignty.
themes.inclusion: Passages calling to regulate big techs, criticising tech oligarchs, or resisting multinational pressure on digital infrastructure.
themes.exclusion: General AI regulation calls without concentration critique (use AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
themes.boundary_cases: Bypassing the UN Scientific Panel also takes AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: A handful of technical oligarchs want to resurrect a version of digital ultra liberalism without rules or transparency.
it would be an unforgivable historical omission not to address the challenge of regulating the big techs and artificial intelligence

themes.label: Tech race bypassing UN scientific panel
themes.definition: Concern that tech companies bypass the UN and its Scientific Panel on AI.
themes.inclusion: Passages referencing the UN or the Scientific Panel on AI as bypassed or central.
themes.boundary_cases: Combined with oligarch critique, code both.

examples.quote: bypassing the United Nations and the scientific panel on artificial intelligence

themes.label: Protecting children and families from algorithms
themes.definition: Companies shift algorithmic harms onto families; national legislation protects children, adolescents and women in the digital environment.
themes.inclusion: Passages on protecting children/families from algorithmic or platform harms.
themes.boundary_cases: Gambling platform harms count only when framed as algorithmic harm to families.

examples.quote: Companies that are aware of the risk of their products are transferring the impossible task of confronting algorithm to the families.
protect children, adolescents, and women in the digital environment

themes.label: AI listed among technologies for partnership
themes.definition: AI named in a list of cutting-edge technologies (Industry 4.0, nanotechnology, 5G) open for partnership, without further discussion.
themes.inclusion: Passages listing AI among technologies for development or partnership.
themes.exclusion: Passages elaborating AI risks or regulation.
themes.boundary_cases: Conditioning partnership on sovereignty and data protection does not make it substantive AI discussion.

examples.quote: 4.0 Industry, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology and 5G technology

value.rationale: Brazil 2026 substantively attacks unregulated big tech and AI oligarchs, defends the UN AI panel and child protection, while Brazil 2020 only lists AI among technologies open for sovereign partnerships.
